Bhishma reveals his intention to Yudhishthira, advising him to lead an attack with Arjuna, Panchalas, and Srinjayas to kill him, as it would be a righteous act leading to heaven.

Satyaki, grandson of Shini, fought with Ashvatthaman, son of Drona; Yudhamanyu fought with Duryodhana and his attendants.
Virata, the tormentor of enemies, led his army and fought with Shalya, son of Sharadvana, who led his army.
Yudhishthira fought with Shalya, king of Madra, a great archer leading his army, while Bhima, under protection, charged towards the elephant corps.
Dhrishtadyumna, prince of Panchala, along with the Somakas, vigorously charged towards the invincible and irresistible excellent warrior Drona.
Vrishasena, the victorious prince with a lion banner, charged towards Abhimanyu, son of Subhadra, who had the Karnikara flower banner.
The sons of Dhritarashtra and other kings together charged towards Shikhandin and Arjuna in battle, eager to kill them.
The two armies fought fiercely, creating a terrifying scene where the earth trembled from the running of warriors.
Seeing Bhishma engaged in battle, both armies clashed together in mixed combat.
The battle was filled with terrifying sounds: conch shells, drums, elephant roars, and lion-like roars of warriors.
The sky became dark with arrows, spears, javelins, and darts from both armies, creating a terrifying scene with dust like clouds and weapon flashes like lightning.
In the great battle, chariots and cavalry collided, elephants killed elephants, and infantry killed infantry.
Like two vultures fighting over a piece of meat, the Kaurava and Pandava clans fought fiercely over Bhishma.

extraction_text: Abhimanyu, along with his army, fought with your son for the sake of Bhishma, O King.
The angry Duryodhana shot nine straight arrows at Abhimanyu in battle, then shot three more arrows at him.
Abhimanyu, filled with rage, hurled a terrifying spear at Duryodhana in battle, like the sister of Death.
Duryodhana, your great warrior son, cut that fearsome spear in two with a razor-edged arrow as it flew swiftly.
Seeing his spear fall, Abhimanyu became extremely angry and shot three arrows at Duryodhana's arm and chest.
Then Abhimanyu shot ten terrible arrows at the irritable Duryodhana's chest.
The battle between Abhimanyu (son of Subhadra) and Duryodhana (bull of the Kuru clan) was terrible yet wonderful, admired by spectators and revered by all kings.

Satyaki shot nine heron-feathered arrows at all vital points of Ashwatthama.
Ashwatthama quickly shot nine arrows, then thirty more arrows at Satyaki's arms and chest.
Satyaki, severely wounded, shot three arrows at Ashwatthama.
Bhurishrava (son of Bahlika) intercepted the great warrior Yuyudhana (Satyaki) with arrows, repeatedly hitting this great archer.
Yuyudhana shot three sharp arrows at Bhurishrava.
Bhurishrava broke Yuyudhana's bow, let out a powerful roar, and shot ten more arrows.
Yuyudhana took another bow and shot seventy-three sharp frog-mouthed arrows at Bhurishrava.
The two great warriors broke each other's bows, killed each other's horses, and fought with swords after their chariots were disabled.
Bhurishrava, filled with rage, shouted 'Stop! You stop!' and struck Yuyudhana's skull with his sword.
Yuyudhana struck Bhurishrava's collarbone with his sharp sword.
Both warriors fell to the ground together after attacking and striking each other fiercely.
Yuyutsu (your son) took Bhurishrava onto his own chariot and carried him away from the battlefield.
Nakula (son of Madri) carried Yuyudhana away from the battlefield.
